# Get-ZbxUserMacro

## SYNOPSIS

Gets the user macros that items and triggers refer to.

## SYNTAX

### All (Default)

## DESCRIPTION

A user macro is a named value, such as {$APP.PORT}, that items, triggers and other fields refer to; a host or template macro overrides a global one. The Get-ZbxUserMacro cmdlet reads them with usermacro.get: all of them up to -Limit, by name with -Name (* and ? are wildcards), by id with -Id or from the pipeline, or with the whole usermacro.get selection in -Filter. -Group, -Host and -Template narrow the result to the user macros of the objects given, each a name, an id or a piped object. It writes ZabbixUserMacro objects, with their related objects when a -Select switch asks for them, or, with -CountOutput, the number of matches; it needs a connection made with Connect-ZbxServer.

## EXAMPLES

### Example 1: List a host's macros

```powershell
Get-ZbxUserMacro -Host 'web-01' | Select-Object HostMacroId, Macro, Value, Type
```

-Host takes a host name, id or object; the result is the host's own macros (not inherited or global ones).

### Example 2: Find one macro on every host of a group, through the pipeline

```powershell
Get-ZbxHost -Group 'Linux servers' | Get-ZbxUserMacro |
    Where-Object Macro -EQ '{$APP.PORT}' |
    Select-Object HostId, Macro, Value
```

A piped host binds -Host by its HostId. Macro names are matched here with Where-Object on the Macro property.

### Example 3: Search macros by part of their name

```powershell
Get-ZbxUserMacro -Host 'web-01', 'db-01' -Search @{ macro = 'APP.' } -SelectHosts |
    Select-Object @{ n = 'Host'; e = { $_.Hosts.TechnicalName } }, Macro, Value
```

-Search is usermacro.get's substring search, keyed by the API field name (macro).

### Example 4: List the global macros

```powershell
Get-ZbxUserMacro -Global | Select-Object Macro, Value, Description
```

-Global reads the server-wide macros (Administration > Macros) instead of host and template macros.
